headline: PM Vishwakarma completes three years with 30 lakh artisans registered under the scheme
fullText:
Ministry of Micro,Small & Medium Enterprises

PM Vishwakarma completes three years with 30 lakh artisans registered under the scheme

Chief Minister of West Bengal Shri Suvendu Adhikari highlighted the State’s Commitment to empower Traditional Artisans

30 Lakh Beneficiaries Registered Under PM Vishwakarma; Around 24.50 Lakh Have Received Basic Skill Training: Union Minister for MSME Jitan Ram Manjhi

Empowering Women Entrepreneurs Key to Building Stronger Families, Communities and a Prosperous Viksit Bharat: MoS Shobha Karandlaje

Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME) celebrated the occasion at Dhono Dhanyo Auditorium in Kolkata, West Bengal

18 SEP 2026 1:00AM by PIB Delhi

The Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India, celebrated the 3rd Anniversary of the PM Vishwakarma at Dhono Dhanyo Auditorium, Kolkata, West Bengal. The occasion marked three years of the Scheme’s implementation and highlighted the Government’s continued efforts to strengthen the livelihoods, skills and entrepreneurial capabilities of traditional artisans and craftspeople.

West Bengal onboarded for implementation of PM Vishwakarma in May 2026, marking an important step towards extending comprehensive support to the State’s traditional artisans and craftspeople. The celebrations in Kolkata underscored the scheme’s significance in empowering Vishwakarmas through skill training, modern tools, institutional credit and market linkages.

On the occasion of the 3rd Anniversary of PM Vishwakarma, an exhibition showcasing the rich traditional arts and crafts of Vishwakarma artisans, was inaugurated by Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi, Union Cabinet Minister, Ministry of MSME, Sushri Shobha Karandlaje, Union Minister of State for MSME, Shri Dipak Barman, Minister of MSME & Textiles, Government of West Bengal and Shri Ashoke Dinda, Minister of State for MSME & Textiles, Government West Bengal. The exhibition provided Vishwakarmas of West Bengal, a platform to showcase their traditional craftsmanship and entrepreneurial skills.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Suvendu Adhikari, Chief Minister of West Bengal, highlighted the importance of extending skill training and credit support to traditional artisans and craftspeople in the State. He expressed his gratitude to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi for the transformative vision behind PM Vishwakarma and acknowledged its significant role in strengthening the livelihood of artisans and craftspeople across the country. Outlining the progress of PM Vishwakarma in West Bengal, he stated that more than 7 lakh applications have been received under the scheme. He stated that Government of West Bengal will expedite provisioning of facilitative support to enable Vishwakarmas avail the benefits under the scheme. The Chief Minister also assured coordinated efforts by the State for effective and timely implementation of PM Vishwakarma across West Bengal in association with Ministry of MSME, Government of India. He called upon the concerned State agencies to strengthen outreach and implementation so that the benefits of the scheme reach every eligible artisan and craftspeople.

He appreciated the implementation of various schemes and initiatives of the Ministry of MSME in West Bengal, noting their contribution to promoting entrepreneurship, generating employment, supporting enterprise development and strengthening the MSME ecosystem in the State. He emphasised that effective implementation of these initiatives would contribute towards realising Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of a Viksit Bharat.

The Union Minister for MSME, Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi, highlighted the achievements of the PM Vishwakarma, launched by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 17th September 2023 to empower traditional artisans and craftspeople through skill training, provisioning of modern toolkit, credit and market support. He stated that 30 lakh beneficiaries have already been registered under PM Vishwakarma, out of which around 24.50 lakh have received Basic Skill Training. 18.15 lakh modern toolkits have been delivered through India Post, while 6.18 lakh Vishwakarmas have received loans up to ₹1 lakh at a concessional interest rate of 5% per annum, amounting to ₹5,297 crore.

Union Minister of State for MSME, Sushri Shobha Karandlaje, congratulated the beneficiaries attending the 3rd Anniversary Celebration of PM Vishwakarma and extended her best wishes for their entrepreneurial journey. She encouraged them to make full use of the opportunities and support available under PM Vishwakarma and strive towards becoming successful entrepreneurs. She noted that the event holds special significance for West Bengal, which joined PM Vishwakarma recently, marking the first programme of Ministry of MSME under this scheme in the State. She emphasised that empowering women entrepreneurs will play a vital role in building stronger families, communities and a prosperous Viksit Bharat.

Shri Dipak Barman, Minister of MSME and Textiles, Government of West Bengal, stated that PM Vishwakarma has emerged as a transformative initiative for traditional artisans and craftspeople, enabling them towards sustainable livelihood and building stronger enterprises. He appreciated the efforts of Government of India to preserve India’s rich artisanal heritage while creating new pathways for artisans to prosper and contribute to economic growth.

Addressing the gathering, Shri Bharat Khera, Secretary, Ministry of MSME, Government of India, highlighted the significant achievements of the Scheme over the past three years and reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to empowering traditional artisans and craftspeople through skill training, provisioning of modern tools, affordable credit and market linkages. He outlined progress under Ministry of MSME schemes and recent reforms aimed at strengthening the sector to enhance competitiveness and create greater opportunities for MSMEs. Highlighting West Bengal’s strategic importance, he stated that the State is emerging as a gateway to the eastern and northeastern regions and a key driver of development, offering significant potential for MSME growth.

Dr. Rajneesh, Additional Secretary & Development Commissioner, Ministry of MSME, Government of India, made a presentation on the PM Vishwakarma highlighting its key features, achievements and comprehensive support extended to traditional artisans and craftspeople through skill training, modern toolkits, credit and market linkages. He highlighted that 30 lakhs beneficiaries have already received benefits under the scheme since its launch on 17th September, 2023 across India and now with onboarding of West Bengal, the Ministry of MSME is committed to full scale roll out of the scheme in the State.

During the 3rd Anniversary celebration event, PM Vishwakarma ID/Certificates, toolkits and cheque of Rs. 1.00 lakh each were distributed to Vishwakarmas of West Bengal.

The event was graced by Shri Ashoke Dinda, Minister of State for MSME and Textiles, Government of West Bengal, Shri Manoj Kumar Agarwal, Chief Secretary, Government of West Bengal and Shri Anoop Kumar Agrawal, Additional Chief Secretary, MSME, Government of West Bengal. Over 2000 Vishwakarmas and Panchayat functionaries from different districts of West Bengal participated in the event along with key officials from the Ministry of MSME, Government of India, Ministry of Skill Development & Entrepreneurship, Department of Financial Services, Ministry of Finance, Government of India, Banks, India Post and officers of Government of West Bengal.

The 3rd Anniversary celebration of PM Vishwakarma marks a significant milestone in efforts of Government of India to facilitate transition of artisans and craftspeople from being rural entrepreneurs to setting up their own enterprise. The event celebrated the motto of PM Vishwakarma i.e. “Samman, Samarthya and Samriddhi”

headline: Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy interacts with EV beneficiaries and distributors from across the country.Highlights India’s transformative journey towards sustainable and self-reliant electric mobility
fullText:
Ministry of Heavy Industries

Union Minister H.D. Kumaraswamy interacts with EV beneficiaries and distributors from across the country.Highlights India’s transformative journey towards sustainable and self-reliant electric mobility

Minister Calls for an inclusive, affordable and economically sustainable transition to electric mobility,Emphasises localisation, innovation, cost competitiveness and global capabilities.

Beneficiaries expressed confidence on government policies for e mobility.

17 SEP 2026 11:24PM by PIB Delhi

Union Minister for Heavy Industries & Steel Shri H.D. Kumaraswamy today interacted with beneficiaries and distributors of electric vehicles (EVs) from across the country at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi. The interaction was organised by the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) to provide a platform for EV beneficiaries, distributors and industry stakeholders to share their experiences, perspectives and insights on the adoption and use of electric vehicles.

The interaction was attended by Shri Kamran Rizvi, Secretary, Ministry of Heavy Industries; Dr. Hanif Qureshi, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Heavy Industries; senior officials of the Ministry; representatives of the automobile industry; EV manufacturers, distributors and dealers; and EV beneficiaries from different parts of the country. Industry representatives included Mr. Sai Giridhar, President, Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA); Mr. Sushant Naik, Chairman – EMG, Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM); and Mrs. Anjali Singh, President Designate, Automotive Component Manufacturers Association of India (ACMA).

The programme highlighted the growing electric mobility ecosystem in the country and the Government’s sustained efforts towards promoting clean, sustainable and self-reliant transportation.Dr. Hanif Qureshi, Additional Secretary, Ministry of Heavy Industries, in his Welcome and Opening Remarks, highlighted the Government’s strong policy push for electric mobility and emphasised that localisation is key to building a resilient and self-reliant automotive ecosystem. He noted that initiatives such as PM E-DRIVE and PLI-Auto are supporting domestic manufacturing of critical EV components.

Government committed to Atmanirbhar Bharat and Viksit Bharat@2047

Addressing the gathering, Shri H.D. Kumaraswamy highlighted India’s transformative journey towards sustainable and self-reliant electric mobility. He extended his greetings to Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on his birthday and acknowledged his continued service to the nation.

The Union Minister reiterated the Government’s commitment to building an Atmanirbhar Bharat and achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047.

Shri H.D. Kumaraswamy appreciated the leadership and vision of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in driving India’s transition towards electric mobility and building a cleaner, greener and self-reliant transportation ecosystem. He also appreciated the efforts of the Ministry of Heavy Industries in implementing various initiatives and schemes aimed at accelerating EV adoption, strengthening domestic manufacturing and creating an enabling ecosystem for electric mobility.

Highlighting the Government’s comprehensive approach to electric mobility, Shri H.D. Kumaraswamy spoke about the PM E-DRIVE Scheme, which supports EV adoption and charging infrastructure, as well as the PLI-Auto and PLI-ACC schemes, which are strengthening domestic manufacturing of advanced automotive technologies and battery cells.

The Union Minister emphasised the need for an inclusive, affordable and economically sustainable transition to electric mobility, supported by robust manufacturing, innovation and a strong ecosystem. He congratulated EV users for contributing to cleaner mobility and reduced crude oil imports and appreciated the industry’s efforts towards producing world-class vehicles with increasing local content.

He called upon all stakeholders to work together to build a seamless, accessible and globally competitive electric mobility ecosystem aligned with India’s national mission.

The Union Minister further emphasised the importance of listening to the experiences of EV users and other stakeholders on the ground. He noted that feedback from beneficiaries and distributors would help in further strengthening policy implementation and addressing emerging requirements across different segments of the electric mobility ecosystem.

Industry representatives share perspectives on evolving EV landscape

The programme was also addressed by key representatives from the automobile industry. Mr. Sai Giridhar, President, Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA); Mr. Sushant Naik, Chairman – EMG, Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM); and Mrs. Anjali Singh, President Designate, Automotive Component Manufacturers Association of India (ACMA) shared their perspectives on the evolving electric mobility landscape and the industry’s experience with the growing adoption of electric vehicles.

EV beneficiaries share ground-level experiences

At the interaction, EV beneficiaries from across India presented diverse perspectives on the use of electric vehicles across different segments of electric mobility.They spoke about how an electric two-wheeler is supporting his daily mobility and livelihood while providing lower running costs.Ms. Sunita Chaudhary, an e-3W driver, spoke about using an electric three-wheeler for her livelihood and the benefits of lower running costs and reduced driving fatigue.They discussed the suitability of electric four-wheelers for everyday passenger mobility and cleaner transportation.The beneficiaries’ perspectives provided valuable ground-level insights into the benefits of electric mobility across personal mobility, livelihoods, public transport and freight movement. They also expressed confidence in continued Government support and enabling policies to further strengthen India’s electric mobility ecosystem and advance a cleaner, greener and more sustainable future

Shri Kamran Rizvi, Secretary, Ministry of Heavy Industries, highlighted India’s rapid progress in electric mobility and said, “Electric mobility is a great opportunity for India to become a global electric mobility player.”

He highlighted key initiatives including FAME I & II, PLI Auto, PLI-ACC, PM E-DRIVE, PM-eBus Sewa (PSM) and the Rare Earth Permanent Magnet Scheme, and called upon industry to focus on cost competitiveness, technology and global capabilities.

The programme reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to advancing India’s Net Zero goals, promoting Atmanirbhar Bharat, strengthening domestic manufacturing and realising the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047 through the development of a robust, sustainable and self-reliant electric mobility ecosystem.

The interaction marked an important step towards strengthening dialogue among Government, industry, distributors and EV users and further consolidating India’s journey towards clean, sustainable and globally competitive electric mobility.

headline: Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Inaugurates SEMICON India 2026; Unveils India’s Ambitious Roadmap for Transition to Semicon 2.0, with Expanded Support for Design, Manufacturing, Packaging, R&D and Talent Development
fullText:
Ministry of Electronics & IT

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Inaugurates SEMICON India 2026; Unveils India’s Ambitious Roadmap for Transition to Semicon 2.0, with Expanded Support for Design, Manufacturing, Packaging, R&D and Talent Development

PM Interacts with Young Chip Designers and Students; Encourages Them to Drive India’s Semiconductor Future

PM Calls upon Global Industry to Partner in Building a Complete Semiconductor Ecosystem in India

PM Launches New Commercial Semiconductor Production Lines: India Moves from Policy to Production

17 SEP 2026 10:36PM by PIB Delhi

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi today inaugurated SEMICON India 2026 to be held from 17-19 September 2026 in New Delhi. Addressing the occasion and highlighting the significance of the event's fifth edition, the Prime Minister extended warm greetings to all participants. He expressed gratitude to the international attendees who had traveled to India to participate in the summit.

Hosted at Yashobhoomi, SEMICON India 2026 features over 600 exhibitors, including approximately 300 international participants, six country pavilions and twelve Indian state pavilions. It also includes a Startup Pavilion and a Workforce Development Zone. On first day, there were about 12,000 visitors at the event.

Shri Ajit Manocha, President & CEO, SEMI, said the global semiconductor market is forecast to reach USD 3 trillion by 2035 and urged India to build indispensable capabilities across key value-chain segments.

Shri Sanjay Mehrotra, CEO, Micron Technology, said commercial DRAM and NAND production is live at Sanand, Gujarat.

Mr. Jochen Hanebeck, CEO, Infineon Technologies, highlighted the company's 2,800+ employees in India, its skilling partnership with NIELIT and opportunities in power semiconductors, smart mobility and automotive electrification.

Dr. Randhir Thakur, CEO & MD, Tata Electronics, confirmed that the construction of Dholera 300mm fab and Jagiroad OSAT facility is on track. He informed that Tata Electronics shall be signing 7 MoUs in the areas including inter-alia semiconductor wafer manufacturing, assembly and test; building advanced semiconductor packaging capabilities; supply of photoresists and advanced chemicals for fab; localization of critical semiconductor materials, and talent development, with Fujifilm, Nexperia, BESI Singapore Pte. Ltd, JSR Corporation etc.

Mr. Toshiki Kawai, CEO, Tokyo Electron, committed support for India's upcoming wafer fabs and advanced packaging facilities and announced a semiconductor training centre in Gujarat next year in partnership with the Government of Japan.

Mr. Benjamin Hein, CEO Electronics, Merck, emphasized that fab viability requires parallel local investment in ultra-pure semiconductor chemicals and gases, safe materials handling and certified domestic suppliers.

Dr. Prabu Raja, President, SPG, Applied Materials, announced 'India Vision 2035': a USD 5 billion investment over the next decade and tenfold expansion of its India-based supply-chain capacity by 2035.

Shri Shesha Varadarajan, COO, Lam Research, announced approximately ₹10,000 crore for the company's first silicon-component manufacturing and vertical ingot-processing plant in India, and said its Semiverse programme has reached over 99 universities.

Mr. Wayne Allan, EVP, ASML, reiterated its partnership with Tata Electronics for lithography solutions at the Dholera fab and said ASML is considering the possibility of integrating Indian suppliers for its global supply chain.

Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, Union Minister for Electronics & IT, Railways, and I&B noted that while foundational groundwork has been done under Semicon 1.0, including 70,000 design engineers trained and EDA tools deployed across 500+ organizations, Semicon 2.0 scales ecosystem development across six comprehensive pillars: Design, Equipment & Materials, Fabs, Advanced Packaging, Applied R&D and Talent.

The Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi interacted with 20 students from academic institutions across the country who presented a memento of 20 chips, designed, fabricated and tested for various applications.

Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi virtually inaugurated commercial production lines at CDIL Semiconductor, Mohali for discrete devices and Suchi Semicon, Surat for packaging. This has resulted in five operational commercial semiconductor ATMP units, alongside Micron, Kaynes, and CG Semi, out of the twelve approved units under Semicon 1.0.

Addressing the gathering, Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi highlighted India’s execution velocity and macro resilience with 7.8% quarterly GDP growth, 3,000 km of operational dedicated freight corridors, a sovereign rating upgrade and a successful BRICS Summit hosted by India. Outlining the relentless momentum of the sector, the Prime Minister highlighted the expansion of the India Semiconductor Mission budget from USD 8 billion in Semicon 1.0 to USD 13.5 billion for Semicon 2.0.

Detailing the vision for a robust domestic supply chain, the Prime Minister urged leaders in equipment, chemicals, gases, and materials to capitalize on the golden opportunities presented by the twelve approved projects and an expanding demand pipeline. "We want the entire ecosystem to grow together,” asserted the Prime Minister.

At the Conference, Secretary, MeitY, Shri S. Krishnan declared that India has "truly arrived" in the semiconductor space, announcing the transition to Semicon 2.0 after committing its initial six-year funding phase in just four years.

MoUs and Strategic Announcements

Strategic MoUs and announcements spanning design, fabrication, packaging, materials, equipment and skills involved Tata Electronics, Kaynes Semicon, Intel, Nexperia, CDIL Semiconductors and their partners. Key outcomes included India's first commercial QFN chip by Suchi Semicon and eInfochips, integration of the India-designed SenseSoC-200 chip into smart meters, six ChipIN Regional Centres and HORIBA India's KOACH Experience Centre.

Addressing the media, Union Minister Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw outlined ‘Semicon 2.0’, marking India’s transition from foundational credibility to comprehensive domestic capability.

India–USA Country Roundtable – Semiconductor & Electronics Ecosystem

The India-USA Country Roundtable brought together government and industry representatives from 64 Indian companies and 52 international organisations. Discussions focused on commercial partnerships, joint ventures, R&D, supply chains and skills across the semiconductor and electronics value chain.

India–Japan Semiconductor Roundtable

The India-Japan Semiconductor Roundtable focused on combining Japan's strengths in equipment, materials and precision manufacturing with India's demand, design talent and expanding manufacturing base through joint ventures, technology transfers, localized supply chains and R&D.

Focused Sessions

The opening day featured focused sessions charting India’s transition from foundational policy planning to large-scale execution across the silicon value chain. These sessions covered AI-enabled chip design and manufacturing, advanced packaging, next-generation manufacturing, equipment R&D and workforce development.

SEMICON India 2026 which runs till September 19th at Yashobhoomi, New Delhi, features more than 600 participating companies and is expected to attract around 50,000 visitors, with representatives from 52 countries, more than 400 executives and over 150 speakers. The exhibition features six Country Pavilions representing Japan, South Korea, Malaysia, the Netherlands, Singapore and Sweden, along with 12 State booths, a Startup Pavilion, Innovation Showcase, Student Hackathon and Workforce Development Pavilion.

### OVERVIEW
Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurated SEMICON India 2026 to launch India’s roadmap for Semicon 2.0, marking a strategic transition from foundational policy planning to large-scale production with significantly increased government funding and new industrial infrastructure.

### KEY HIGHLIGHTS
*   **Event & Timeline:** SEMICON India 2026 is scheduled for 17-19 September 2026 at Yashobhoomi in New Delhi, featuring over 600 exhibitors and approximately 12,000 visitors on the first day.
*   **Funding Increase:** The India Semiconductor Mission budget has been raised from USD 8 billion for Semicon 1.0 to USD 13.5 billion for Semicon 2.0.
*   **Infrastructure Projects:** Tata Electronics is constructing the Dholera 300mm fab and Jagiroad OSAT facility, having signed seven MoUs covering wafer manufacturing, advanced packaging, and talent development.
*   **Manufacturing Milestones:** Micron Technology has activated commercial DRAM and NAND production lines in Sanand, Gujarat, while CDIL Semicon and Suchi Semicon have had their commercial production lines virtually inaugurated.
*   **Investment Commitments:** SPG announced a USD 5 billion "India Vision 2035" investment and a target for tenfold expansion of supply-chain capacity by 2035.

fullText:

‘Seva Sankalp, Khadi Mahotsav-2026’ to be Celebrated Nationwide Till October 17

“Seva Sankalp, Khadi Mahotsav-2026 Will Carry Forward the Resolve of 25 Years of Service and Good Governance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi through Jan Bhagidari”: KVIC Chairman

KVIC Disburses ₹289 Crore Margin Money Subsidy to 3,366 PMEGP Beneficiaries; Five Digital Initiatives Launched

17 SEP 2026 10:28PM by PIB Delhi

The Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India, inaugurated the "Seva Sankalp, Khadi Mahotsav 2026" on Thursday, marking the birth anniversary of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, from the KVIC campus at Gandhi Darshan, Rajghat. The commemoration will be celebrated nationwide from September 17 to October 17, 2026, with public participation. The chief guest, Shri Manoj Goyal, Chairman, KVIC, inaugurated the event. On the occasion, former Delhi Mayor Shri Jai Prakash, representatives of Khadi institutions, artisans, PMEGP beneficiaries, trainees, officers and employees of KVIC, as well as artisans and other participants who joined online from across the country, were present. During the event, the artisans cut a cake with #AshirwadKaDiya and lit 25 lamps of "Sankalp se Siddhi" to symbolize Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's 25 years of service, good governance, and public participation.

Shri Goyal said that service, good governance, and public participation have been key principles ​​in Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's 25 years of public life. Inspired by this spirit, KVIC will spread the message of Khadi, Swadeshi, employment, and self-reliance through the 'Seva Sankalp, Khadi Mahotsav-2026'. He said that Khadi is not just a fabric, but a symbol of self-respect, employment, rural economy, and Swadeshi. Under the Prime Minister's leadership, campaigns like 'Vocal for Local', 'Atmanirbhar Bharat', and 'Local to Global' have given a new identity to local products and rural entrepreneurship.

During the programme, machines and toolkits were distributed to artisans from Delhi and the North East regions. Shri Goyal said that these are not just equipment, but new opportunities for employment, self-reliance, and respect for artisans. Margin money subsidy of ₹289 crore was also disbursed under the PMEGP. This will establish 3,366 new projects across the country and create employment opportunities for approximately 37,026 people. Bank loans worth approximately ₹873 crore have been provided for these projects. At the event, 5,000 new PMEGP units were launched online. He said the objective of PMEGP is to transform youth, women, and rural entrepreneurs from job seekers to job creators.

The program marked the launch of the E-Commerce Portal, PMEGP Online EDP Portal, PMEGP Online EDP Mobile App, Hindi Vaibhav Portal, and KVIC Digital 2.0, aimed at making KVIC's digital services more accessible and effective. Also, 760 individual, group workshops, and renovated stores were inaugurated online across the country, and a Khadi and Village Industries Exhibition was organized. Activities such as the inauguration of a selfie point, a live demonstration of spinning the charkha, and the "Swadeshi Sankalp" campaign were also organized at the venue. Certificates were distributed to candidates trained in various skill development courses. Cleanliness activities were organized at the KVIC office complex at Gandhi Darshan, and Chairman, KVIC, Shri Manoj Goyal, planted a sapling, promoting environmental protection and a clean campus.

Under the "Seva Sankalp, Khadi Mahotsav 2026," cleanliness drives, tree plantations, Khadi Yatras, the Swadeshi Sankalp pledge, awareness programs, artisan dialogues, and training programs will be organized across the country til 17th October. Schools, villages, towns and Khadi institutions will be associated to these activities. Shri Goyal said that KVIC's effort is that this festival should not remain just a departmental programme but should become a campaign for the people and a festival of public participation. He said that there should be dialogue of Khadi in every school, talk of village industries in every village, talk of Swadeshi in every market.

Seva Sankalp, Khadi Mahotsav will also be linked with the 'Swachhata Hi Seva 2026' campaign running from 17th September to 17th October. This year the theme of Swachhata Hi Seva campaign is 'Participation in Cleanliness, Clean India, Developed India'. Shri Goyal said, "Cleanliness is service, Swadeshi is service, providing employment is service, and respecting artisans is service." He called upon artisans, Khadi institutions, PMEGP beneficiaries, youth, and the KVIC family across the country to actively participate in the "Seva Sankalp, Khadi Mahotsav 2026."

On this occasion, Shri Manoj Goyal opined that under the guidance of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Khadi has achieved a new dimension. Today, Khadi has become a powerful medium to realize the resolve of Atmanirbhar Bharat, Vocal for Local, Local to Global, and Developed India 2047. He said that Khadi is not just a fabric, but a source of livelihood for millions of artisans and weavers, a symbol of India's cultural heritage and sustainable development.

Khadi and Village Industries sector has made unprecedented progress due to Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's visionary thoughtfulness and policies, he added. In the financial year 2025-26, the turnover of the Khadi and Village Industries sector exceeded ₹1.87 lakh crore, while the total income generated through this sector was ₹1.87 lakh crore. More than 20.4 million people are employed. He expressed confidence that the sector will achieve its target of ₹2.51 lakh crore in turnover in the coming years.

headline: ‘Aashirwad Ka Diya’ symbolises hope and self-reliance for beneficiaries
fullText:
Ministry of Food Processing Industries

‘Aashirwad Ka Diya’ symbolises hope and self-reliance for beneficiaries

Union Minister Chirag Paswan interacts with beneficiaries at Seva Sankalp Abhiyan–Seva Diwas in Thane

17 SEP 2026 10:15PM by PIB Delhi

The “Aashirwad Ka Diya” programme was organised at Niyojan Bhawan, District Collector’s Office, Thane, as part of the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan–Seva Diwas initiative of the Ministry of Food Processing Industries. The programme brought together farmers, FPO members, women beneficiaries, entrepreneurs, food-processing units and departmental representatives.

The programme was attended by Hon’ble Union Minister for Food Processing Industries Shri Chirag Paswan, Hon’ble Member of Parliament Shri Naresh Maske, Thane Deputy Mayor Shri Krushna Patil, along with Shri Preet Pal Singh, Joint Secretary, Ministry of Food Processing Industries; Shri Krishna Panchal, Collector, Thane; Shri Ranjit Yadav, Chief Executive Officer, Zilla Parishad, Thane; Shri Remandeep Chowdhary, Director; Director, Agriculture Processing and Planning; District Superintendent of Agriculture, Thane; and senior departmental officials.

A key highlight was the direct interaction of Shri Chirag Paswan with beneficiaries of various Ministry initiatives, including PMFME, PMKSY and PLI. The Minister listened to their experiences and enquired about the impact of government support on their businesses and livelihoods, including the employment opportunities generated through their projects.

Food processing: a major opportunity

The programme also highlighted the immense potential of the food-processing sector. While India once faced limitations in food production, the country today has a strong and diverse agricultural production base, creating significant scope for processing, preservation and value addition.

The need of the hour is therefore to give greater impetus to food processing and build a strong and integrated value chain that connects farmers, FPOs, entrepreneurs, processors, industry and markets.

The emerging participation of entrepreneurs from both rural and urban India reflects this changing landscape. Entrepreneurs from different backgrounds are increasingly coming forward to establish food-processing enterprises and build products that represent the spirit of Brand Bharat.

‘Aashirwad Ka Diya’ – a symbol of hope

The lighting of the “Aashirwad Ka Diya” was the central feature of the programme. The diya symbolised hope, opportunity, confidence and self-reliance in the lives of beneficiaries.

It represented the collective strength of the food-processing ecosystem—farmers producing quality raw material, FPOs bringing collective strength, women converting skills into enterprise, entrepreneurs undertaking processing and value addition, and industry providing technology, scale and market opportunities.

Beneficiaries shared their experiences and explained how government initiatives had helped them strengthen their enterprises, create employment and move towards greater economic self-reliance.

Maharashtra’s contribution acknowledged

Maharashtra has consistently played an important role in the implementation of initiatives of the Ministry of Food Processing Industries and in strengthening the participation of farmers, FPOs, women and entrepreneurs in the sector.

Shri Chirag Paswan expressed his pleasure at interacting with beneficiaries from Maharashtra and appreciated the opportunity to work with the state’s farmers, entrepreneurs and other stakeholders.

The programme reinforced the message of Seva Sankalp Abhiyan–Seva Diwas—that the true purpose of public service is realised when opportunities created through government initiatives reach people and translate into enterprise, employment, value addition and better livelihoods.

The “Aashirwad Ka Diya” thus became a symbol of a larger vision: to transform India’s agricultural strength into greater value, stronger enterprises and new opportunities, while carrying the light of entrepreneurship and self-reliance to more families across the country.

headline: Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission inaugurates 6th National Pharmacovigilance Week with focus on rational use of medicines
fullText:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission inaugurates 6th National Pharmacovigilance Week with focus on rational use of medicines

6th National Pharmacovigilance Week to be observed across the country from 17–23 September 2026

Week-long campaign to sensitise healthcare professionals, researchers and public on Adverse Drug Reaction (ADR) reporting and encourage active participation in pharmacovigilance

17 SEP 2026 10:11PM by PIB Delhi

The 6th National Pharmacovigilance Week (NPW) was inaugurated at the Padmashri Nitya Anand Auditorium Hall, ALRC Building, Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission (IPC), Ghaziabad, today. IPC serves as the National Coordination Centre for the Pharmacovigilance Programme of India (NCC-PvPI). Being observed from 17–23 September 2026 across the country, the 6th NPW is themed “Promoting Rational Use of Medicines through Pharmacovigilance – A Step Towards Safer Healthcare”. The week-long campaign aims to sensitise healthcare professionals, researchers and the public about the importance of adverse drug reaction (ADR) reporting and encourage active participation in pharmacovigilance.

The inaugural ceremony was attended by Dr. Rajiv Bahl, Director General, ICMR (virtually); Dr. V. Kalaiselvan, Secretary-cum-Scientific Director, IPC; Dr. Jai Prakash, Officer-in-Charge, PvPI; Prof. Sangeeta Sharma, IHBAS; Shri Aditya Kumar Mamgain, Deputy Secretary, MoHFW; and along with other dignitaries and stakeholders.

Dr. Rajiv Bahl, Director General, Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), stressed the importance of building adequate capacity to verify, assess and analyse safety reports, enabling pharmacovigilance data to effectively inform regulatory and clinical actions.

Dr. V. Kalaiselvan, Secretary-cum-Scientific Director, Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission, Ghaziabad, in his remarks, highlighted the need to strengthen the pharmacovigilance network at the grassroots level, with an aspiration for every Aspirational District to have at least one ADR Monitoring Centre (AMC) and one Medical Device Monitoring Centre (MDMC). He also emphasised greater utilisation of pharmacovigilance data, including exploring opportunities for drug repurposing and using safety data to support and promote the rational use of medicines.

The inaugural session also featured remarks by Prof. Sangeeta Sharma, Institute of Human Behaviour & Allied Sciences (IHBAS), New Delhi; Dr. Abdul Nasser, Cardiac Anaesthesiologist, Max Hospital, Vaishali; and Shri Aditya Kumar Mamgain, Deputy Secretary, Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India. Video messages were delivered by Shri Tukaram Mundhe, Commissioner, FDA Maharashtra and Dr. Shanthi Pal, Team Lead, Pharmacovigilance, World Health Organization (WHO).

A key highlight of the programme was the release of Volume 16, Issue 2 (2026) of the PvPI Newsletter, reflecting the programme’s continued efforts towards strengthening pharmacovigilance, promoting rational medicine use and enhancing public awareness on medicine safety.

The technical sessions focused on strengthening medication and patient safety. Prof. Sangeeta Sharma spoke on “Pharmacovigilance and Rational Use of Medicines: Two Pillars of Medication Safety”, while Dr. Abdul Nasser addressed “Beyond Medicines: Role of MvPI in Strengthening Patient Safety”, highlighting the complementary role of pharmacovigilance and materiovigilance.

The 6th NPW reinforces the call for greater ADR reporting and the effective use of pharmacovigilance data to promote safer and rational use of medicines.

headline: Central Government is Committed to the Equitable Development of Every Region and State in the Country: Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh
fullText:
Ministry of Panchayati Raj

Central Government is Committed to the Equitable Development of Every Region and State in the Country: Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh

25 Years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's Public Life are Like a Golden Era of Development and Transformation for the Country: Union Minister of State Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel

An Interaction Program with Beneficiaries of the PM 'SVAMITVA' Scheme and Fisheries Scheme was Held at NDDB, Anand

17 SEP 2026 10:04PM by PIB Ahmedabad

Under the joint aegis of the Union Ministry of Panchayati Raj and the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, a special interaction program with beneficiaries of the 'SVAMITVA' Scheme and Fisheries Scheme, as well as a property card distribution ceremony under the SVAMITVA scheme, was held today at the National Dairy Development Board (NDDB) Auditorium in Anand.

Union Minister of Panchayati Raj, Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh was specially present as the Chief Guest, and Union Minister of State for Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel was present as the Special Guest on this occasion.

Speaking at the program, Union Minister Shri Rajiv Ranjan Singh stated that the entire life of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has been dedicated to the service of Mother India. During his successful tenure as the Chief Minister of Gujarat, he accomplished the monumental task of bringing Narmada waters to every corner, permanently solving the state's major water problem. It was due to this journey of development and popularity that the people of the country entrusted him with the leadership of the nation in 2014. Today, under the Prime Minister's leadership, India is moving forward with the resolve to become a 'Viksit Bharat' by 2047. The Central Government is committed to the equitable development of every region and state of the country. Uniting all states into a single thread without any political discrimination to make the country self-reliant is the main objective of the Prime Minister.

The Union Minister further stated that property-related issues were the biggest cause of violence and disputes in rural areas. Owing to the Prime Minister's foresight, the 'SVAMITVA Scheme' was launched, under which title deeds (cards) for their land/properties are handed over to villagers through drone surveys. Currently, more than 3 crore SVAMITVA cards have been distributed across the country. On the basis of these cards, villagers can now easily obtain loans from banks, freeing them from exploitation by usurers. The work on the second phase of this scheme across the country, including Gujarat, is in its final stage, which is proving to be a blessing in bringing social harmony and economic prosperity to villages.

Outlining the development in the fisheries sector, the Minister stated that the livelihood of approximately 6 crore people in the country is connected with the fisheries sector. After 2014, the Central Government took historic decisions for this sector, such as the Blue Revolution, PM MSY (PM Matsya Sampada Yojana), and the creation of a separate Ministry of Fisheries. Despite global economic challenges and tariff issues, under the guidance of the Prime Minister, this sector has been taken to new heights by formulating policies for Free Trade Agreements (FTA) and deep-sea fishing.

On this occasion, Union Minister of State Prof. S. P. Singh Baghel stated that the 25 years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's public life are not merely a period of time, but are like a golden era of development and transformation for the country. After making Gujarat a role model as its Chief Minister, he has brought light into the lives of crores of citizens across the country as Prime Minister through various schemes such as poverty alleviation, electricity, housing, toilets, Ayushman Card, Mudra Scheme, and PM-KISAN. He proved that service to the nation is paramount. Because of his governance, India is today moving towards the 'Golden Era of Indian Politics'.

The Minister stated that the 'SVAMITVA Scheme' and the 'Blue Revolution' have brought a revolutionary transformation in the upliftment of rural India. By providing property cards under the SVAMITVA scheme, ownership rights have been granted in rural areas, bringing an end to land disputes and domestic quarrels between brothers, as well as making it easier for people to receive financial assistance.

During the event, property cards were distributed to rural beneficiaries under the 'SVAMITVA' scheme at the hands of dignitaries. Along with this, direct interactions were held with beneficiaries of the fisheries scheme and the SVAMITVA card scheme to discuss the benefits of government schemes. Beneficiaries of the SVAMITVA scheme and PM Matsya Sampada Yojana also presented their experiences regarding the benefits they received.

The program was attended in large numbers by Chairman of the National Dairy Development Board Dr. Meenesh Shah, Joint Secretary of the Panchayati Raj Department Shri Amit Agrawal, Director Dharmendra Ji, District Development Officer Ms. Devahuti, officials of the district administration, as well as beneficiaries of the Matsya Sampada Scheme and SVAMITVA Scheme.

fullText:
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare

Union Health Ministry Commemorates World Patient Safety Day 2026 at NIHFW; with Focus on Safe NCD Care

A Structured and Time-Bound Approach to Quality Assurance is Critical for Patient Safety: Smt. Aradhana Patnaik, Additional Secretary & Mission Director (NHM)

Strengthening Patient Safety Critical in Addressing Growing Burden of NCDs: Smt. Patnaik

National Patient Safety Pledge was Administered, Reaffirming Collective Commitment to Safer and Quality Healthcare

Technical Programme Highlights Safe NCD Care and State-led Innovations in Patient Safety

18 SEP 2026 8:07AM by PIB Delhi

Union Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India, commemorated World Patient Safety Day 2026 at the NIHFW Auditorium, New Delhi, with the theme “Safe Care for Noncommunicable Diseases (NCDs)”. The national observance focused on strengthening patient safety and quality of care across the continuum of NCD care and brought together policymakers, healthcare leaders, public health experts, clinicians, quality managers, development partners and representatives from States and Union Territories.

Addressing the gathering, Smt. Aradhana Patnaik, Additional Secretary & Mission Director (NHM), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, reiterated the Government of India’s commitment to strengthening patient safety, improving quality of care and building safer health systems across the country. She emphasized that patient safety cannot be the responsibility of a single programme or department and needs to be embedded across the health system, particularly in the prevention, diagnosis, treatment and long-term management of noncommunicable diseases.

Highlighting the growing burden of NCDs, Smt. Patnaik noted that nearly 63 per cent of all deaths in India are attributed to NCDs, making patient safety an important component of healthcare delivery. Referring to recent achievements in public healthcare, she highlighted that 96 per cent of immunizations and 90.6 per cent of institutional deliveries, as reported under NFHS-6, are being conducted through public health facilities. She stressed the need to further strengthen quality and safety practices within healthcare institutions, particularly in patient referrals and continuity of care, to ensure timely access to appropriate services and improved health outcomes.

Calling upon States and Union Territories to accelerate quality improvement efforts, Smt. Patnaik emphasized the need for a clear roadmap and action plan to achieve 100 per cent NQAS certification of Ayushman Aarogya Mandir–Sub Health Centres (AAM-SHCs) by March 2027, followed by certification of Ayushman Aarogya Mandir–Primary Health Centres (AAM-PHCs). She underscored that a structured and time-bound approach to quality assurance would be critical for institutionalising a culture of patient safety across all levels of care.

The inaugural session concluded with the administration of the National Patient Safety Pledge, reaffirming the collective commitment of healthcare stakeholders towards ensuring safer care and strengthening the quality of healthcare delivery across the country.

The technical programme thereafter featured a dedicated seminar on “Safe Care for Noncommunicable Diseases (NCDs)”, bringing together eminent experts to deliberate on key patient safety challenges and approaches across the continuum of NCD care. The discussions covered the burden of harm in NCD care, strengthening patient safety in NCD services, leveraging digital health for patient safety, ensuring safe NCD care across clinical pathways with a focus on co-morbidities, and promoting medication safety in NCD care.

The programme subsequently focused on translating policy into practice through discussions on patient safety implementation and quality improvement initiatives across States. Participants shared State-led innovations and best practices, including Jharkhand’s model for comprehensive geriatric diabetic and hypertensive screening, Kerala’s Hridhyaragam initiative for prevention and control of NCDs, and Rajasthan’s SETU online referral application. These experiences highlighted the importance of context-specific approaches, knowledge sharing and adoption of effective practices to strengthen patient safety at different levels of healthcare delivery.

India has also been strengthening the institutional framework for quality and patient safety through initiatives such as the National Quality Assurance Standards (NQAS) and the National Patient Safety Implementation Framework. Against this backdrop, the observance of World Patient Safety Day 2026 provided an important platform for bringing together stakeholders, sharing experiences and best practices, and reinforcing a culture of patient safety across all levels of healthcare delivery.

The national observance reflected the Government of India’s continued commitment to improving quality of care and advancing patient safety as an integral component of Universal Health Coverage. Through dialogue, knowledge sharing and collective action, the event contributed to strengthening healthcare systems and advancing the vision of “Safe Care for Life.”

The event was attended by senior officials from the Ministry of Health & Family Welfare and partner institutions, including Shri Sibin C., Joint Secretary (Policy), MoHFW; Prof. (Dr) Pragya Sharma, Executive Director, NHSRC; Shri Deepak Soni, Director (NHM); Dr Binod Kumar Patro, Director, NIHFW; and Dr Rajiv Pathni, Advisor (Quality & Patient Safety), NHSRC, along with policymakers, healthcare leaders, technical experts, development partners and representatives from States and Union Territories.

Considering the need to generate high-frequency labour force indicators with enhanced coverage, the sampling methodology of the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) has been revamped from January 2025. Further, to maintain uniformity with the international practice of reporting labour force indicators, the survey period of PLFS has been shifted from the July–June cycle (i.e., agricultural year) to the January–December cycle (i.e., calendar year) from 2025. The modified PLFS sampling design is envisaged to address the following objectives:

to estimate the key employment and unemployment indicators (viz. Labour Force Participation Rate, Worker Population Ratio and Unemployment Rate) on a monthly basis for rural and urban areas in the Current Weekly Status (CWS) at all-India level

to extend the coverage of the Quarterly results of PLFS to rural areas and thereby producing quarterly estimates covering both rural and urban areas of India in the Current Weekly Status (CWS)

to estimate important employment and unemployment indicators in both usual status (ps+ss) and CWS for rural and urban areas annually

The PLFS sampling design from 2025 onwards has considered districts as the basic stratum for the majority of the geographical area, thereby facilitating the generation of district‑level estimates. Prior to 2025, the PLFS sampling design was based on NSS Regions as the basic stratum and was therefore not specifically designed to generate district‑level estimates.

B. Methodological caveats

This bulletin represents the first release of district‑level estimates under the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), based on the revised sampling design adopted from January 2025. The estimates presented herein are based on the sampling frame as constituted at the time of sample selection and may not reflect subsequent changes in district boundaries, bifurcation or nomenclature.

While the estimates provide valuable insights into labour market conditions at the district level, they are subject to the limitations inherent in sample surveys. Users are advised to exercise due caution while interpreting the estimates, taking into account the associated sampling variability and Relative Standard Error (RSE). It may be noted that comparison with earlier NSS-region-based estimates is not appropriate, as the present survey design is oriented towards district‑level representation.

C. Conceptual Framework of Key Indicators

The bulletin presents key labour force indicators at basic stratum level namely, Labour Force Participation Rates (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR), Unemployment Rate (UR) and persons Not in Employment, Education or Training (NEET). These indicators, along with the ‘Usual Status’ and ‘Current Weekly Status’ measurement approaches, are defined as follows:

Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR): LFPR is defined as the percentage of persons in the labour force (i.e., working or seeking or available for work) in the population.

Worker Population Ratio (WPR): WPR is defined as the percentage of employed persons (i.e., persons who were engaged in any economic activity) in the population.

Unemployment Rate (UR): UR is defined as the percentage of persons unemployed (i.e., persons who, owing to lack of work, had not worked but either sought work through different channels or expressed their willingness or availability to work) among the persons in the labour force.

Not in Employment, Education or Training (NEET): NEET is defined as the percentage of persons who are not in employment, education or training during the reference period in the population.

Activity Status - Usual Status: The activity status of a person is determined on the basis of the activities pursued by the person during the specified reference period. When the activity status is determined on the basis of the reference period of last 365 days preceding the date of survey, it is known as the usual activity status of the person.

Principal activity status (ps): The activity status on which a person spent a relatively long time (major time criterion) during last 365 days preceding the date of survey was considered the usual principal activity status of the person.

Subsidiary economic activity status (ss): The activity status in which a person, in addition to his/her usual principal status, performs some economic activity for 30 days or more for the reference period of last 365 days preceding the date of survey, was considered the subsidiary economic activity status of the person.

Activity Status - Current Weekly Status (CWS): The activity status determined on the basis of a reference period of last 7 days preceding the date of survey is known as the current weekly status (CWS) of the person.

headline: WOAH PVS–PPP Targeted Support Workshop on “FMD-Free Zone Development in India” concludes with focus on strengthening State Action Plans and Public–Private Partnerships
fullText:
Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying

WOAH PVS–PPP Targeted Support Workshop on “FMD-Free Zone Development in India” concludes with focus on strengthening State Action Plans and Public–Private Partnerships

18 SEP 2026 3:56PM by PIB Delhi

The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying (DAHD), Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India, in collaboration with the World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH), organised a three-day PVS–PPP Targeted Support Workshop on “FMD-Free Zone Development in India” from 15–17 September 2026 at the National Agricultural Science Complex (NASC), New Delhi. The workshop brought together representatives from the DAHD, 12 State Animal Husbandry Departments, experts from WOAH, Paris, CDDL/RDDLs, NDDB, ICAR Research Institutions, industry, livestock value-chain stakeholders and technical experts to strengthen the pathway towards establishing FMD-free zones and compartments in India.

The workshop was aimed at supporting national and state stakeholders in refining and strengthening their FMD-free zone and compartment action plans through technical analysis, peer learning, public–private partnership (PPP) design and alignment with WOAH standards and official recognition requirements.

The Inaugural Session was graced by Shri. Naresh Pal Gangwar, Secretary, AHD and WOAH Delegate of India in presence of Dr Naveena B. Maheswarappa, Animal Husbandry Commissioner, DAHD, Dr Divakar Hemadri, ADG (Animal Health), ICAR, New Delhi and Ms. Barbara Alessandrini, Head, Capacity Building Department, WOAH, Paris.

Shri. Naresh Pal Gangwar, Secretary, AHD in his address highlighted India’s journey for FMD Control in India. He informed that, India has made substantial progress in FMD control under the Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme. Under the Government’s flagship FMD control programme, the country has invested in large-scale vaccination, animal identification, surveillance, laboratory strengthening and disease reporting. He mentioned about the Department’s objective under the Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme to control and ultimately obtain FMD freedom by 2030. Administration of more than 147.16 crore FMD vaccine doses till date, benefiting around 8.04 crore farmers and decline in FMD outbreaks from 132 in 2019 to 40 in 2025 and 20 till August 2026 and decline in NSP antibody positivity to 8.1% in 2025 were also highlighted.

He also informed that this workshop is a continuation of the WOAH PVS-PPP Targeted Support which was held in India during 2025 and thanked WOAH for their continued partnership and technical support through the PVS–PPP Targeted Support programme. He further added that the Department has developed the guidelines for creation of FMD free compartments in India with extensive rounds of consultation with stakeholders. Further the Department for the first time has also come up with the Minimum Standards of Veterinary Infrastructure in India in 2025 and the Department is supporting the States under the Support to States for Capital Investment (SASCI) framework, to address infrastructure and system-readiness gaps identified by States. He also urged to have a discussion on the emerging threat of SAT Serotypes of FMD and highlighted India’s preparedness to deal with such exotic serotypes.

He emphasised that, India has demonstrated a sustained national FMD control and the next step is to prove and maintain freedom in defined populations. With WOAH's technical guidance and the combined efforts of States, Veterinary Services, laboratories, industry and exporters, we can build FMD-free zones and compartments that are scientifically credible, operationally sustainable, digitally traceable and capable of supporting greater confidence and trade.

On the first day WOAH experts provided an overview of the WOAH Performance of Veterinary Services (PVS) Pathway and the PVS–PPP approach, WOAH requirements for recognition of FMD-free zones, surveillance and post-vaccination monitoring, international experience from Brazil, and opportunities for public–private engagement.

A key component of the workshop was a series of practical group exercises involving public and private stakeholders from the nine priority States. The second day focused on co-designing solutions to address identified bottlenecks. Discussions covered vaccination systems and engagement with the vaccine industry, surveillance and diagnostic partnerships, animal identification and traceability, producer organisations and value-chain integration, as well as investment and financing models.

The final day focused on validation of State-level action plans. Representatives of the nine priority States presented their proposed action plans, followed by technical feedback from WOAH experts and other specialists. The presentations provided an opportunity to refine interventions related to surveillance, vaccination, laboratory preparedness, traceability, biosecurity, movement control, veterinary infrastructure and PPP engagement.

The workshop emphasised that PPP engagement should extend beyond financial participation and encompass the full animal-health value chain, including vaccine supply and delivery, diagnostics, animal identification and traceability, producer organisations, dairy and livestock value chains, veterinary service delivery and risk communication. The approach is intended to create stronger ownership, accountability and sustainability of FMD-free zone initiatives.

The three-day deliberations culminated in the refinement of State Action Plans and identification of priority technical interventions and opportunities for public–private partnership (PPP) in FMD-free zone and compartment development. In the concluding session, Dr. Naveena B. Maheswarappa, Animal Husbandry Commissioner, expressed appreciation for the valuable technical guidance provided by the WOAH team of experts and acknowledged the active participation and constructive contributions of the State Animal Husbandry Departments and other stakeholders.

Dr. Maheswarappa expressed confidence that the States would translate the outcomes of the workshop into clear, evidence-based and time-bound action plans for the progressive development of FMD-free zones and compartments, with strengthened collaboration and meaningful engagement of the private sector.

The initiative represents an important step towards India's national objective of achieving FMD-free status by 2030. The strengthened State Action Plans, supported by WOAH standards and appropriately designed public–private partnerships, are expected to provide a structured pathway for progressive development, maintenance and eventual recognition of FMD-free zones and compartments in India.

headline: India advancing towards Viksit Bharat@2047 with resilience, strength, innovation, inclusive development & compassion: Raksha Mantri
fullText:
Ministry of Defence

India advancing towards Viksit Bharat@2047 with resilience, strength, innovation, inclusive development & compassion: Raksha Mantri

18 SEP 2026 3:29PM by PIB Delhi

Raksha Mantri Shri Rajnath Singh has said that the Government is serving the nation with a special focus on fostering resilience, determination, compassion, innovation, strength, inclusive prosperity and a strong sense of national identity among citizens to realise the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047. Addressing an event in Kochi, Keralam, on September 18, 2026, he asserted that under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, India is advancing on the path of development by drawing inspiration from India’s centuries-old values such as courage to persevere, security and protection of citizens, spirit of service, determination to achieve goals, compassion, inspiring future generations, strengthening national capabilities, and ensuring inclusive prosperity & global leadership.

Raksha Mantri highlighted that before 2014, India faced significant challenges such as corruption and misgovernance which had weakened the morale of the people, and the nation’s progress in the last 12 years has been shaped by its ability to face adversity with confidence and convert challenges into opportunities. “Over the last 12 years, the world has faced a pandemic such as COVID-19 and witnessed several wars, which have had a profound impact on the global economy. Despite global challenges, we are moving steadily on the path towards becoming a self-reliant and developed nation,” he said.

Reiterating the Government’s commitment towards the protection and security of citizens from evil forces, Shri Rajnath Singh stated that Operation Sindoor is proof of India’s willingness to cross the border to eliminate those who threaten the sovereignty and integrity of the country. He added that Naxalism, too, has been brought to an end.

On the Government’s aim to continuously bolster indigenous capabilities, Raksha Mantri stated that indigenous defence production, which was just Rs 40,000 crore in 2014, has now reached nearly Rs 1.80 lakh crore. He added that defence exports have risen from nearly Rs 600 crore to around Rs 40,000 crore, with Indian equipment reaching around 100 countries.

Voicing the nation’s resolve to work tirelessly towards its goals with courage and determination, Shri Rajnath Singh described youth as the country’s greatest strength. “Our youth are building start-ups, creating unicorns, developing drones, building hydrogen trains, and making rockets and satellites. They are leaving no stone unturned to make India a developed nation,” he said.

Raksha Mantri added that guided by the virtue of compassion, the Government is working to improve the lives of the people, pointing out that over the past 10 to 12 years, more than 250 million people have been lifted out of poverty. He also stated that whether it is the success of India’s democracy or the success of its welfare schemes, India today serves as a source of inspiration to the world. He spoke about UPI, which is the world’s largest real-time payment system, and has been adopted by more than 11 countries. He mentioned the schemes such as PM SHRI, Ayushman Bharat, Lakhpati Didi, Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana, Jal Jeevan Mission, and Ujjwala Yojana, which have made development more inclusive.

Shri Rajnath Singh noted that India has become a source of hope for the world as it has achieved several targets set to fight climate change ahead of schedule, and provided free vaccines to the people in the country & sent more than 300 million vaccines to 100 countries during COVID-19. He stressed that India has emerged as a civilisational leader as today the world celebrates International Yoga Day. India is now providing leadership to the world through initiatives such as the International Solar Alliance and the Global Biofuels Alliance, he added.

Raksha Mantri underlined that India’s development journey is not limited to economic growth, but also involves strengthening national confidence and moving beyond the colonial mindset. Under PM Modi’s leadership, India is witnessing a cultural and civilisational renaissance, he said. Highlighting the importance of civilisational and cultural heritage, he stated that the country’s modernisation should go hand-in-hand with an appreciation of its cultural traditions. “’Sarva Dharma Samabhava’ or equal respect for all faiths has always been at the heart of our civilisational ethos. And yet, because of Western secularism, our Dharma was made to appear as communalism, tradition as backwardness, belief as fanaticism, and faith as superstition,” he added.

Shri Rajnath Singh emphasised the importance of making the younger generation more aware of India’s history, culture and heritage. Greater awareness among youth, he said, would contribute to stronger national consciousness and help build confidence in India’s place in the world. He called upon the youth to contribute to India’s economic, social and technological transformation, saying that a confident, capable and socially inclusive India can emerge as a developed nation and play a greater role in shaping the future of the world.

On the crucial role of media in today’s times, Raksha Mantri stated that journalism is rightly called the fourth pillar of democracy, terming an independent & impartial press as one of the strongest instruments for ensuring accountability. “The role of the media is not merely to report the news. It is also to ask difficult questions, bring the truth before the people, and hold those in power accountable,” he said.

headline: BIMSTEC Energy Centre Organises Five-Day Capacity Building Programme on New & Emerging Technologies in Power Sector
fullText:
Ministry of Power

BIMSTEC Energy Centre Organises Five-Day Capacity Building Programme on New & Emerging Technologies in Power Sector

Programme brings together participants from seven BIMSTEC Member States for technical capacity building and knowledge sharing

18 SEP 2026 3:23PM by PIB Delhi

The BIMSTEC Energy Centre (BEC) organised a five-day Capacity Building Programme on “New & Emerging Technologies in Power Sector (Generation, Transmission, Distribution & End Use)” from 14 to 18 September 2026 in Bengaluru in hybrid mode under the aegis of Ministry of Power, Government of India.

The programme was inaugurated on 14 September 2026 by Sh. Ghanshyam Prasad, Executive Director, BEC and Chairperson, Central Electricity Authority (CEA), Government of India, along with Sh. Pankaj Kumar, Joint Secretary (Transmission), Ministry of Power, Government of India.

The Inaugural Session was also attended by Smt. J Sreedevi, Director General, Central Power Research Institute (CPRI), Sh. Asit Singh, Member Secretary, Southern Regional Power Committee (SRPC), Sh. M S Hejib, Executive Director, POWERGRID SRTS-II, and Sh. T Srinivas, Executive Director, Southern Regional Load Despatch Centre (SRLDC), GRID-INIDIA.

Participants from Bhutan, India, Sri Lanka and Thailand attended in person, while Bangladesh, Myanmar and the BIMSTEC Secretariat, Dhaka participated online. The programme provided a platform for technical capacity building, exchange of national experiences and sharing of best practices in the rapidly evolving power sector.

The programme covered key emerging technologies across the power sector, including Renewable Energy, Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), Green Hydrogen, Carbon Capture, Utilisation and Storage (CCUS), Long Duration Energy Storage, Small Modular Reactors (SMRs), Smart Grids, advanced grid operation technologies, Artificial Intelligence (AI) in power systems and the impact of Data Centre loads. Advanced transmission technologies such as FACTS, HTLS conductors, Dynamic Line Rating and Grid-Forming Converters, along with the India Energy Stack, were also covered.

The programme combined classroom sessions with technical and industrial visits to major power-sector facilities in and around Bengaluru, including the 2500MW HVDC Kolar POWERGRID Station, Ohmium International Green Hydrogen Electrolyzer Gigafactory, POWERGRID’s RTAMC, SRLDC/REMC Control Rooms, CPRI Laboratory Facilities and Hot Line Training Centre (HLTC), NPTI.

The programme concluded on 18 September 2026 with a Valedictory Session, in the presence of Sh. Bhagwan Sahay Bairwa, Chief Engineer, CEA. The session included sharing of key learnings, country perspectives and participant feedback, followed by certificates and acknowledgements.

The programme forms part of BEC’s continuing capacity-building and knowledge-sharing initiatives aimed at promoting regional energy cooperation among BIMSTEC Member States. This particular program provided a strong foundation for greater cooperation in power-system planning, renewable integration, energy storage, transmission technology, knowledge sharing and electricity trade in BIMSTEC Region.

About BIMSTEC Energy Centre (BEC)

The BEC became operational in Bengaluru on 1 April 2025 and serves as a Centre of Excellence for regional energy cooperation, promoting sustainable development, energy security and energy integration among BIMSTEC (Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi Sectoral and Technical Cooperation) Member States Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Myanmar, Nepal, Sri Lanka & Thailand.
